catalog_quote: It [ɣi-Sirə (B41)] probably includes as sub-dialects both ɣi-Varamə, spoken in three villages inland from Gamba, and ɣi-Vungu, West of Mouila. [...] like all the other dialects of B 40, except Ngubi, ɣi-Sirə is a so-called "tone-case" language [...] in the Summer of 1989 I worked with two speakers of ɣi-Varamə, father and son [...] In the father's speech I was able to detect two kinds of type D nominals as in ɣi-Sirə, although the tonal manifestation was somewhat different [...] I obtained 19 words in sub-class D1 and 18 in sub-class D2 and was able to verify that the former were reflexes of *HH and the latter of *HL as in ɣi-Sirə.

In the father's speech I was able to detect two kinds of type D nominals as in ɣi-Sirə, although the tonal manifestation was…
new_statements.relation_note: Tone only (nominal tone classes, *HL split, H-spread rule proposed for the group); no statement on stress or accent for Varama or for B40 generally.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Varama has lexical tone of the B40 type: nominals fall into tone-classes A/B/C/D (underlying °LL, °HL, °LH, °HH, reflexes of Proto-Bantu *LL/*HL/*LH/*HH), established in a post-verbal test frame; an older speaker still separates D1 (<*HH) from D2 (<*HL) by a slight tonal difference, a younger speaker has merged them; as in the rest of B40 (except Ngubi) the surface tone pattern of a nominal varies with its position in the utterance ('tone-case'). Nothing is said about stress/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: D1/D2 distinction lost in the younger speaker's speech; Ngubi is the only B40 variety said not to be 'tone-case'.
new_statements.identity_note: Not linked to bara1362 in Glottolog (Blanchon's B40 papers sit under Sira/Sangu or the sira1270 node). The Varama data are explicitly 'ɣi-Varamə, spoken in three villages inland from Gamba' = Bavarama of the Ndogo lagoon/Bongo area (Ogooué-Maritime), i.e. B402 bbg; speakers named in fn. 3 (Mutsinga-Souza Jean-Félix, Souza Yeno Henri-Joseph). Blanchon treats Varama as a probable sub-dialect of ɣi-Sirə (B41). The PDF font renders ɣ as 'ﬁ' and ə as '2' in extracted text.

sources.citation: Alewijnse, Bart; Nerbonne, John; van der Veen, Lolke J. & Manni, Franz. 2007. A computational analysis of Gabon varieties. Proc. RANLP Workshop on Computational Phonology, pp. 3-12
sources.note: Varama/B402 is NOT among the 53 ALGAB sample sites (B40 = B41 Sira, B42 Sangu, B43 Punu, B44 Lumbu only). Blanket remark on the ALGAB Gabon database, p. 2: 'Stress is not marked in the database because it is predictable in all varieties. It is usually placed systematically on the first syllable on the noun stem, while sometimes straightforward penultimate stress is used. No stress contrasts have been found (within single varieties).' Not a statement about Varama.
